notes: All samples are small, self-authored teaching examples written for this harness. They are not copied from real CVE code or any production codebase.

pairs.explanation: The username is concatenated directly into the SQL string, so an attacker can break out of the quoted value and change the query's logic (classic SQL injection).
pairs.fix_summary: Use a parameterized query so the driver treats the username as data, never as SQL syntax.

pairs.explanation: A Statement is executed with a query built by string concatenation, allowing injection through the username parameter.
pairs.fix_summary: Use a PreparedStatement with a ? placeholder and bind the value with setString.

pairs.explanation: Second-order SQL injection: the username is stored with a safe parameterized insert, then read back from the database and interpolated into a new query with an f-string. Storage did not sanitize it -- the value was attacker-controlled at write time and stays attacker-controlled when it comes back out.
pairs.fix_summary: Bind the retrieved value as a query parameter instead of interpolating it; data from the database is data, never SQL syntax.

pairs.explanation: DocumentBuilderFactory is used with default settings, so a crafted XML document can define external entities and make the parser read local files or make network requests (XXE).
pairs.fix_summary: Disallow DOCTYPE declarations entirely and turn off XInclude and entity expansion on the factory.

pairs.explanation: pickle.loads on attacker-controlled bytes (a base64 cookie value) executes arbitrary code during unpickling; pickle data is a program, not a data format.
pairs.fix_summary: Serialize session data as JSON and parse it with json.loads, which cannot execute code.

pairs.explanation: yaml.load with the default (full) Loader constructs arbitrary Python objects from the document, so a crafted profile document executes code during parsing -- the same failure class as pickle, one import away.
pairs.fix_summary: Use yaml.SafeLoader, which only constructs plain dicts, lists, and scalars.

pairs.explanation: The user-supplied filename is joined to the base directory unchecked, so '../../etc/passwd'-style input escapes the intended directory.
pairs.fix_summary: Strip directory components with basename, resolve the final path, and verify it still lives under the base directory before opening it.

pairs.explanation: baseDir.resolve(fileName) trusts the caller-supplied name; a name containing '..' segments resolves outside baseDir.
pairs.fix_summary: Normalize the resolved path and reject anything that does not start with the base directory.

pairs.explanation: The server fetches any URL the caller supplies, so it can be pointed at internal metadata endpoints or intranet services (SSRF).
pairs.fix_summary: Parse the URL and only fetch https URLs whose host is on an explicit allowlist.

pairs.explanation: The allowlist check validates only the original URL. The redirect target from the Location header is fetched without re-validation, so an allowlisted host (or an attacker page on one) can bounce the server-side request to a link-local metadata endpoint or an intranet service.
pairs.fix_summary: Disable automatic redirect following and re-validate every hop: each redirect target must itself be an allowlisted https URL before it is fetched.

pairs.explanation: A live-looking API key is embedded in source code, where it leaks through repos, logs, and screenshots and cannot be rotated without a deploy.
pairs.fix_summary: Read the key from an environment variable (or a secrets manager) at runtime instead of storing it in code.

pairs.explanation: The production database password is a string constant in the codebase; anyone with source access has the credential.
pairs.fix_summary: Load the password from the environment with System.getenv at runtime.

pairs.explanation: MD5 is a fast, unsalted hash, so stolen password hashes can be brute-forced or rainbow-tabled at billions of guesses per second.
pairs.fix_summary: Use a slow, salted password KDF (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with a per-password random salt and a high iteration count).

pairs.explanation: DES has a 56-bit key that is brute-forceable, and ECB mode leaks plaintext patterns because identical blocks encrypt identically.
pairs.fix_summary: Use AES in GCM mode, which provides confidentiality and integrity with a modern key size.
